LESSON: HUMAN RIGHTS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Political Developments and Governance
Topic 5.2: Human Rights
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Human Rights, part of Political Developments and Governance in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 8 SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How can we promote respect for Children’ Rights in the community? 2. How can effective communication foster respect for Human Rights?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. sign terms related to human rights,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Human Rights in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. explore how human rights can be respected and protected in the community,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Human Rights in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. describe the process of effective communication on human rights issues,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Human Rights in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. outline the Children’s Rights in Kenya,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Human Rights in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. demonstrate ways in which children are protected against violation of their Rights in Kenya,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Human Rights in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

F. recognise the responsibility of the society in protecting human rights. ●

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Human Rights in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Human Rights together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
● Social Justice: learners foster fairness and justice among themselves as they brainstorm on how human rights can be respected and

protected in the community.

● Respect: learners exhibit value of human dignity when designing an “issue tree” and use it to investigate the root causes, effects and

possible solutions to the violation of human rights.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Safety and Security: learners become aware of protection of children against violation of their rights.

Link to other subjects:

Religious Education: learners apply knowledge on promoting human dignity in the society as they learn about human rights.

Suggested Learning Resources:

print resources, digital resources, approved textbooks, the Kenyan constitution,
